description: The downstream half of koine's namespace defect. `https://koine.dev` is UNREGISTERED (verified 2026-08-11: DNS could not resolve) and it is the KCB manifest EXTENSION URI — the stable key by which a consumer identifies the KCB manifest entry inside an A2A AgentCard's `capabilities.extensions[]`. An unregistered hostname used as an identifying URI is squattable, with no recovery once implementations have shipped it. koine is migrating the namespace to a **w3id.org permanent identifier** (`https://w3id.org/koine/kcb/manifest/<version>`) under `koine:75-w3id-namespace-migration`, with a normative dual-accept transition window. agora pins the old string in at least SIX places, and one of them is the hard part: `schemas/src/agent-card.ts` (`KCB_MANIFEST_EXTENSION_URI`), `schemas/src/agent-card.test.ts`, `provider-router/src/agora_provider_router/manifest.py`, `provider-router-erl/src/apr_manifest.erl` (`?EXTENSION_URI`), `docs/quickstart.md`, and — the one that makes this a real tasklist rather than a find-and-replace — `provider-router-erl/test/apr_conformance_SUITE_data/python-surface.json`, the **byte-for-byte conformance corpus** that pins both routers' emitted manifest bytes and must be REGENERATED by `capture_python_surface.py`, not hand-edited. Both routers must move in the same change or the conformance suite goes red, which is the gate working correctly. Implement the transition koine specifies: agora EMITS the w3id form and ACCEPTS both during the window (any consumer-side matching in `clients/sdk/`, `registry/`, and `console/` must recognise the legacy URI as identifying the same extension), with the legacy form deprecated on sight. PARKED until koine:75 merges — the URI's exact final form is koine's to fix, and migrating to a guessed string would be a second defect. Unpark and run when koine:75 lands.

userStories.title: Move the emitted extension URI in all three languages at once
userStories.description: The URI is pinned in TypeScript, Python, and Erlang, and the three are asserted against each other. Move them together or the gates go red — which is exactly what they are for.
acceptanceCriteria: `KCB_MANIFEST_EXTENSION_URI` in schemas/src/agent-card.ts, `KCB_MANIFEST_EXTENSION_URI` in provider-router/src/agora_provider_router/manifest.py, and `?EXTENSION_URI` in provider-router-erl/src/apr_manifest.erl all carry the w3id form exactly as koine:75 fixes it — read from koine's capability-bus.md, never guessed.
schemas/src/agent-card.test.ts asserts the new value, and docs/quickstart.md's example card shows it.

The version segment convention is preserved: whatever KCB version segment koine's spec carries after its bump is the one agora emits, and the pin moves with `schemas/src/versions.ts` (see chief/70) rather than independently of it.
`make check` is green across every gate.

userStories.title: Regenerate the byte-for-byte conformance corpus
userStories.description: provider-router-erl/test/apr_conformance_SUITE_data/python-surface.json pins both routers' emitted manifest bytes and contains the old URI twice. It is generated, and must be regenerated.
acceptanceCriteria: python-surface.json is regenerated by `provider-router-erl/test/apr_conformance_SUITE_data/capture_python_surface.py` — NOT hand-edited — and the regeneration command is recorded in the commit body.
`apr_conformance_SUITE` passes: the Erlang and Python surfaces still answer with identical bytes after the move, proving both routers moved and neither drifted.

The regenerated corpus differs from the previous one ONLY in the extension URI (and any version segment that moved with it); any other diff is investigated and explained before the change lands, because an unexplained corpus diff means something else changed too.
The capture was run with the same environment scrubbing the suite applies, so the corpus stays a function of the fixture rather than of the capturing host.

userStories.title: Accept both URIs for the transition window
userStories.description: koine specifies a dual-accept window: producers emit the new form, consumers accept both. agora is a consumer as well as a producer — the SDK, the registry, and the console all match on this string.
acceptanceCriteria: Every consumer-side match on the extension URI (clients/sdk/, registry/, console/, and anything in schemas/ that identifies the manifest entry) recognises BOTH the legacy koine.dev URI and the w3id URI as identifying the same KCB manifest extension, so a peer that has not yet migrated is still discoverable.
The dual-accept behaviour is TESTED with a card carrying the legacy URI and a card carrying the new one, both resolving to the same manifest.
The legacy acceptance is marked deprecated in code and docs with the end condition koine's spec states — not left as a permanent tolerance, which is how a transition window becomes forever.
The SDK's enumerated public API (`SDK_API`) is updated if a new export is required, since index.test.ts fails on drift.
